source_row.item_data_json: {"options":{"A":"Begin with the face and upper body, proceed downward, and perform perineal care last.","B":"Perform perineal care first because the most contaminated area should be completed before cleaner regions.","C":"Wash the feet and legs first, then the upper body, and perform perineal care midway through the bath.","D":"Choose the sequence according to convenience as long as the washcloth is rinsed between body regions."}}
source_row.rationale: The NCBI Bookshelf nursing-assistant procedure describes a head-to-toe bath sequence that begins with the face and neck and leaves perineal care until the end to reduce pathogen transfer from a more contaminated area. Option A follows that sequence. Option B starts with the perineum and increases cross-contamination risk. Option C places perineal care before cleaner regions are finished. Option D disregards the clean-to-dirty sequence.
